sources.title: The role of transportation in the persuasiveness of public narratives
sources.publisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 79(5), 701-721

concepts.definition: The use of narrative to communicate.
The state of being absorbed in a story, with imagery, emotion and focused attention.

questions.q: Name the components of a story.
questions.a: For example character, goal, obstacle, stakes, turning point and resolution.

questions.q: What did Green and Brock (2000) find about highly transported readers?
questions.a: They noticed fewer flaws in the story and held more story-consistent beliefs.
